assessment.task: N02-T6 NXDOMAIN against the real resolver via libslirp
assessment.summary: 43/100 unchanged. The libslirp case now also resolves the reserved name missing.invalid: app A gets NotFound in-guest, the kernel pins two UDP queries and one additional rejected request, and the runner requires exactly one NXDOMAIN without addresses bound to that query on the wire. The resolver is the host-configured one reached through QEMU user networking; no physical NIC, timeout, truncation or stale-response case is covered, so N02 remains open and earns no points.

gates.title: Independent UEFI boot
gates.acceptance: The custom loader transfers control to the custom kernel; normal boot, missing/corrupt kernel, and timeout cases are checked natively.

gates.title: Independent memory management and fault boundaries
gates.acceptance: Custom page tables and frame management, W^X, guard stacks, and invalid mappings are checked in the fixed QEMU profile.

gates.title: Isolated preempted processes
gates.acceptance: Ring-3 processes have separate address spaces; an application fault does not stop the other test processes.

gates.title: Capabilities and bounded IPC
gates.acceptance: Rights reduction, generations, revocation, user-copy handling, and bounded Message320 IPC have native negative and lifecycle tests.

gates.title: General process and service management
gates.acceptance: Non-fixture applications can start and stop through bounded APIs and services can restart; dependencies and resources are released correctly.

gates.title: Multiple processor cores
gates.acceptance: SMP scheduling, synchronization, interrupts, and address-space switching work under concurrent load on the supported profile.

gates.title: Resource management under pressure
gates.acceptance: Memory, CPU, IPC, and handle exhaustion remain bounded per application; the usable system recovers without kernel failure.

gates.title: Native read, write, and flush
gates.acceptance: Service-bound READ/WRITE/FLUSH operations use real virtio I/O; success is reported only after controlled completion.

gates.title: Journal and cold recovery
gates.acceptance: A bounded object journal survives native interruptions, revision checks, full storage, and cold recovery with an independent disk oracle.

gates.title: Names and domain-bound catalog
gates.acceptance: Native GET/PUT/DELETE/RENAME/LIST preserve names, contents, and domain boundaries, including interrupted renames.

gates.title: Space reuse and scalable volumes
gates.acceptance: Storage safely reuses deleted space and continues beyond the former 32-record limit; crash-consistent compaction and quotas are tested.

gates.title: Documents of useful size
gates.acceptance: Large documents and streams exceed the former 128-byte probe limit; bounded buffers, full volumes, and partial writes are tested.

gates.title: Collections, metadata, and edit history
gates.acceptance: Native object collections, persistent metadata, and recoverable revisions support daily Material tasks with consistent transactions.

gates.title: Uncertain I/O without kernel panic
gates.acceptance: The current M6c catalog service returns controlled Unknown results for native WRITE/FLUSH failures, closes further access, and does not replay uncertain writes; there is no false ACK or kernel panic and other processes remain alive. Fault injection, cold recovery, disk-oracle checks, and normal M6c/M6b regressions are stored. This does not extend the historical M6b observer with a new error-handling claim.

gates.title: General storage recovery after failures
gates.acceptance: A usable system remains responsive during disk failure, timeouts, corruption, and resource exhaustion; explicit recovery choices prevent silent data overwrite.

gates.title: Backup, recovery, and data export
gates.acceptance: A user can create, verify, restore, and export independent recovery copies in documented formats; loss and conflict scenarios are tested.

gates.title: First independent device path
gates.acceptance: Custom virtio block transport, bounded DMA/MMIO access, reset behavior, and driver/service crashes are tested natively in QEMU.

gates.title: Keyboard, mouse, and USB
gates.acceptance: Common input and USB devices work on the documented reference profile; hotplug and invalid device responses remain bounded.

gates.title: Graphics output and audio
gates.acceptance: Native graphics output, required GPU functionality, and audio meet documented usability and latency budgets on physical reference hardware.

gates.title: Network hardware and connections
gates.acceptance: Ethernet, Wi-Fi, and the agreed Bluetooth functions work on supported hardware, including disconnect, resume, and driver-failure paths.

gates.title: Power management and sleep/wake
gates.acceptance: ACPI/power management, sleep/wake, shutdown, and thermal/battery functions are measured and recoverable on supported hardware.

gates.title: Physical support matrix
gates.acceptance: Several predefined representative PC configurations pass the documented hardware matrix; DMA/IOMMU boundaries and limitations are explicit.

gates.title: Native compositor and session
gates.acceptance: The custom kernel runs an interactive graphical session with render and input chains, window/surface isolation, and controlled compositor recovery.

gates.title: Responsive daily interaction
gates.acceptance: Keyboard, pointer, focus, clipboard, and application switching are usable natively and meet measured interaction budgets.

gates.title: Material from open to save
gates.acceptance: Users open, edit, rename, and organize real native documents; permissions, history, and location remain understandable and correct.

gates.title: Native accessibility
gates.acceptance: Keyboard-only use, screen reader support, scaling/zoom, contrast, and reduced motion work in the native chain; user task tests are recorded.

gates.title: Settings, search, and recovery
gates.acceptance: Native system settings, local search, account/session management, and understandable error/recovery paths work consistently.

gates.title: Polish validated with users
gates.acceptance: Representative users complete agreed core tasks; friction, errors, and visual inconsistencies are measured and resolved within product budgets.

gates.title: Native packet and transport stack
gates.acceptance: The operating system's network service processes real packets and bounded IP/TCP/UDP connections; malformed input, backpressure, and shutdown are tested.

gates.title: Configuration and everyday internet
gates.acceptance: Address configuration, name resolution, routes, network transitions, and required internet protocols work on real authorized connections.

gates.title: Native authenticated transport
gates.acceptance: Maintained cryptography/TLS with the documented hybrid PQC choice works natively, including peer verification, negative handshakes, and no silent insecure fallback.

gates.title: Enforceable network permissions
gates.acceptance: Process and destination permissions, revocation, and helper routes are enforced natively and observed in traffic; no unintended listening ports exist.

gates.title: Entropy and key management
gates.acceptance: Native cryptographic entropy and key lifecycle, with recovery restricted to manifest-bound management ingress. Native positive management recovery and negative ordinary-app authorization tests remain required.

gates.title: Authenticated personal storage
gates.acceptance: Content and sensitive metadata are protected natively; tampering, replay/rollback within the threat model, and key loss are tested.

gates.title: Signed updates and rollback
gates.acceptance: Authentic updates, interruption, downgrade attacks, and recovery to a valid previous version are tested end to end.

gates.title: Trusted boot and distribution chain
gates.acceptance: Image/boot verification, key rotation, and dependency/build provenance are bounded for the release profile and independently reviewed.

gates.title: Targeted independent security review
gates.acceptance: External experts examine kernel, service, DMA, parser, and capability boundaries; blocking findings are resolved and selected invariants are machine-checked where appropriate.

gates.title: Native privacy contract
gates.acceptance: Applicable LP tests pass on the independent OS, including no telemetry/cloud fallback, local AI, and separated app/download permissions; remaining risks are published.

gates.title: Publicly documented application API and SDK
gates.acceptance: A reproducible SDK builds ordinary applications for the independent OS; API/ABI versions, sandbox behavior, and errors are documented and tested.

gates.title: Install and update applications
gates.acceptance: Packages from multiple sources can be installed, removed, and updated with provenance checks; installation does not grant broad capabilities.

gates.title: Application permissions and tool integration
gates.acceptance: Native applications use Material objects through visible, revocable task permissions; extensions and helper processes cannot bypass those boundaries.

gates.title: Useful everyday applications
gates.acceptance: At minimum, internet use, document editing, media, and file exchange work through suitable native applications or controlled ports; realistic user tasks are tested.

gates.title: Native end-to-end encrypted NAS storage
gates.acceptance: Client and NAS roles on the independent OS pair with verified identity; names and content are unreadable to the NAS administrator, including failure and attack paths.

gates.title: Automatic synchronization and conflicts
gates.acceptance: Previously authorized peers resume automatically; offline edits, conflicts, and LAN/internet transitions preserve permissions and do not silently lose data.

gates.title: Multiple devices and key lifecycle
gates.acceptance: Devices can be securely added and revoked; key rotation, concurrent writers, and recovery work without vendor key escrow.

gates.title: Offer, revoke, and remove storage
gates.acceptance: The native NAS administrator manages quotas and revokes guest authority/removes local copies without guest consent or decryption keys; old sessions do not revive.

gates.title: Useful local system AI
gates.acceptance: At least the agreed core AI tasks run on the local device with bounded context, separate model downloads, and tested network denial; limited resources never cause silent cloud fallback.

gates.title: Local quantum execution on the independent OS
gates.acceptance: The local simulator/job interface runs natively with quotas, cancellation, and reference circuits; host simulation and physical QPU support remain separately labeled.

gates.title: Installation and accessible recovery
gates.acceptance: A user can install, upgrade, and independently recover the OS on supported hardware using controlled preserve/wipe options; a practical test passes.

gates.title: Long-term stability and performance budgets
gates.acceptance: Predefined duration, workload, energy, memory, latency, and data-integrity budgets are met on physical hardware with no known blocking usability defects.

gates.title: Reproducible release and maintenance
gates.acceptance: Independent reproduction, licenses/SBOM, release and patch policy, responsible reporting channel, support, and applicable accessibility/privacy obligations are concretely arranged.

delivery_review.scope: All 30 criteria open at the reviewed main source are covered below. The 21 previously accepted criteria retain their existing acceptance evidence and are outside this implementation inventory. B01 is accepted by this reassessment; the other 29 remain open. This inventory records delivered slices and remaining clauses, not release readiness or all remaining engineering effort.

criteria.remaining: Substantial native independent-copy and recovery work is proven, but a user-facing production copy/restore/export chain and full L2 integration remain incomplete. No S09 acceptance increase is justified.

requirements.description: Create and verify an independent recovery copy
requirements.observation: v1 archive export to a second disposable virtio disk, host verification and source-disk checks pass in the 26-stage native gate. Destination service core and independent disk oracle exist on main.
requirements.remaining: The available native path is an explicitly test-only fixture. Production destination service, trusted selection/portal and per-operation enforcement are not connected natively.

requirements.description: Restore recovery copies with the documented fidelity
requirements.observation: v1 cold restore with the original source disk absent is native-tested; native INSTALL preserves source provenance for its fixed fixture. Host restore_native_l2 implements multi-version/provenance restoration and uncertain-outcome handling.
requirements.remaining: Full L2 archive export/cold-restore pipeline has no native caller. Planned l2-export/l2-restore/l2-corrupt/l2-used stages are absent from PLAN; L2 live revisions/stamps remain destination-local by the approved rule.

requirements.description: Export in documented independent/interchange formats
requirements.observation: Native v1 archive and ustar export are implemented with independent Python decoding; archive v2 format and host code add bounded history/provenance support.
requirements.remaining: User-facing export destination workflow is missing; ustar is intentionally lossy and does not substitute for native history/provenance restore.

requirements.description: Test loss and conflict scenarios
requirements.observation: 26-stage gate includes corrupted archive, occupied/conflicting destination, full/absent/small/wrong archive disk, intentional cuts and cold recovery; host regressions preserve uncertainty after BEGIN/APPEND/COMMIT/collection/cleanup.
requirements.remaining: Negative evidence covers bounded fixtures and host destination core, not the still-missing production destination/portal boundary or planned L2 archive cold-restore workflow.

criteria.remaining: Define and test the reference device set and physical controller support; cover applicable error/hotplug paths on that set.

requirements.description: Common keyboard and mouse input on the documented reference profile
requirements.observation: Native display/input and USB boot-protocol keyboard/mouse reports pass in the defined QEMU fixture.
requirements.remaining: HW-FR target is unset; physical controllers are rejected by the current qemu-xhci allowlist.

requirements.description: Bounded unplug and hotplug without stale authority
requirements.observation: Both keyboard and mouse same-port reattach pass. Mouse unplug with a held button, generation retirement, slot reuse and stale work rejection are covered by PR480's USB cases.
requirements.remaining: Only bounded QEMU root-port fixtures; general hubs, IRQ operation, controller reset and long-lived product policy handoff remain outside acceptance.

requirements.description: Invalid device responses and DMA remain bounded
requirements.observation: xHCI fault/no-DMAR/read-only cases and strict descriptor/report parsing exist; the fixture retains retired pages and checks canaries.
requirements.remaining: Physical invalid-response matrix is absent; some malformed responses have host-only evidence; canaries detect writes and do not themselves prevent them.

criteria.remaining: Complete product audio/GPU interfaces and agreed budgets, then physical measurement and practical usability trials.

requirements.description: Native graphics output
requirements.observation: GOP framebuffer display and four DISPI modes have pixel-oracle evidence; PR480 repeats positive raw33 and expected unsupported-device refusal raw35.
requirements.remaining: No physical GPU/display test, EDID/timing coverage or product ring-3 mode-change service.

requirements.description: Required GPU functionality on reference hardware
requirements.observation: The reference contract treats GOP as baseline while required acceleration/device families still need selection.
requirements.remaining: Required GPU feature set and physical target are not decided; no hardware acceptance.

requirements.description: Native audio including bounded failure/recovery
requirements.observation: All five kernel-only virtio-snd cases pass at PR480: normal, no-device, access-platform refusal, fence-reinit and quarantine, each raw33. H03-T3c source hardening is included.
requirements.remaining: PCM/WAV emulator output is not audible hardware playback; ring-3 audio broker/app capability and native audio service remain absent. Configuration changes after DRIVER_OK remain open.

requirements.description: Usability and latency budgets on physical reference hardware
requirements.observation: No physical budget acceptance record exists in the hardware matrix.
requirements.remaining: Freeze budgets and measure actual output, workload/underrun behavior, latency and usability on the selected physical configuration.

criteria.remaining: Native virtual networking advances must be retained as evidence; H04 still requires named supported physical hardware and the agreed connection families.

requirements.description: Ethernet on supported hardware
requirements.observation: virtio-net provides real native packets in the QEMU profile; no accepted physical NIC is recorded.
requirements.remaining: A supported physical NIC and driver remain required; e1000e is unsupported in the current matrix and no e1000e driver path exists.

requirements.description: Wi-Fi and agreed Bluetooth functions
requirements.observation: These device families remain owner scope decisions and have no supported driver rows.
requirements.remaining: Select chipsets, firmware/licensing and exact Bluetooth scope; implement and test physical paths.

requirements.description: Disconnect, resume and driver-failure paths preserve bounded behavior
requirements.observation: Native link down/up clears retained RX, preserves down-window no-send invariants and reacquires a fresh neighbor; link-storm exhaustion resets/latches the device. Network integration adds reconnect/configuration work.
requirements.remaining: Hardware unplug/cable/radio/sleep-resume is untested; the original link fixture does not exercise in-flight TX at the down edge.

criteria.remaining: Preserve the completed QEMU work while requiring physical firmware, power/battery scope and complete product resume evidence.

requirements.description: ACPI shutdown and safe flush/recovery
requirements.observation: Latest native-power performs five S5 shutdowns and corrupted-DSDT refusal; the power-system gate includes normal, flush-error and flush-timeout plus cold recovery.
requirements.remaining: Physical ACPI firmware and app-level save/discard/cancel shutdown flows are not accepted.

requirements.description: Sleep/wake, rejected wake and power-plan recovery
requirements.observation: PR480 covers three S3 cycles plus corrupt FACS, stale-token, unarmed-wake and FACS-end refusal. Expected exits are33/39/37/37/39, all without timeout.
requirements.remaining: QMP wake under one QEMU/OVMF policy only; physical wake sources, AML _PTS/_WAK, wider firmware and SMP/FPU product resume remain unverified.

requirements.description: Post-wake devices and services remain usable or fail closed
requirements.observation: Current 12-stage power gate passes S3 loss refusal, RNG reinit and held-completion quiescence plus cold recovery; broker device-access latches/counters are present.
requirements.remaining: The entropy delivery demonstration is kernel-driven; block reinitialization and complete product device/session survival are not established. Some latches are source/counter checks only.

requirements.description: Thermal/battery and physical power measurements
requirements.observation: OD-HW-POWER and HW-FR remain open; no measured thermal or battery support record exists.
requirements.remaining: Define the hardware power profile and measure thermal/battery, wake reliability and energy on physical devices.

criteria.remaining: No point can be awarded for protocols or emulation alone; multiple named physical configurations must pass.

requirements.description: Several predefined representative physical PC configurations
requirements.observation: No representative physical PC configurations have been selected: HW-FR target is null. VM-FR and VM-VMW are emulation profiles; nine hardware owner decisions remain open.
requirements.remaining: Select the representative PC set and settle required device families and measurement/capture arrangements.

requirements.description: Each configuration passes the hardware matrix
requirements.observation: All HW-FR entries are pending or unsupported with evidence_level none; H06-T4 prepares protocols and signature validation only. H06-T3 adds a read-only native-hw-inventory kernel/loader pair that emits the HW-INV markers; it passes two QEMU configurations against QMP query-pci and configured CPUID/DMAR, and its inventory is rejected as a virtual capture. H06-T5 makes every terminal path of that pair halt without port 0xF4 (four QEMU fixtures). H06-T6 packs it into a deterministic raw GPT/FAT32 image with a recorded SHA-256 that boots in QEMU as a disk.
requirements.remaining: Physical operators, authorization and signed actual runs remain missing; host validation of evidence format proves no device support.

requirements.description: DMA/IOMMU boundaries and limitations are explicit
requirements.observation: The matrix names trusted kernel transport versus unsupported isolation. VT-d-contained qemu-xhci exercises bounded DMA and refusal fixtures.
requirements.remaining: No general physical DMA/IOMMU acceptance or user-driver isolation across the representative configurations.

criteria.remaining: Core input/clipboard/switching now has strong native evidence, but the original acceptance also requires measured budget compliance, which has not been established.

requirements.description: Native keyboard, pointer and focus operation
requirements.observation: Current #480 source passes 66-phase window sessions at 100% and 200%, including fault/restart and input/focus checks.
requirements.remaining: These runs prove the supported QEMU session, with interaction-budget compliance still a separate unmet clause.

requirements.description: Native clipboard and application switching
requirements.observation: The source-bound window gate covers clipboard behavior, recovery and peer operation; both 18-phase switcher100/200 runs pass raw33.
requirements.remaining: No additional functional blocker is identified in the bounded tested slice; usability/performance-budget completion is not inferred from passing scripted cases.

requirements.description: Meet measured interaction budgets
requirements.observation: u02-latency-baseline-20261123 records three successful native TCG runs and host-observed input-to-verified-image intervals.
requirements.remaining: No interaction budget or reference profile is preregistered. n=3 per phase does not meet the documented 20-samples-per-stratum rule; timings include QMP, polling and screendumps, not guest scanout latency.

criteria.remaining: Real native document/library operations are delivered; native permission refusal part2 and remaining understandable-history/error behavior prevent whole-criterion acceptance.

requirements.description: Open, edit, rename and organize real native documents
requirements.observation: Current #480 library-write gate runs ten phases, then cold-reopen runs four phases with independent disk/image and source binding; standard Materiaal/window evidence also passes.
requirements.remaining: The demonstrated scope is real native documents in the supported fixture session; it does not confer complete permission or human-understanding acceptance.

requirements.description: Show and enforce correct understandable document permissions
requirements.observation: #455/#480 part1 adds the native read-only grant/profile and compiles it in CI. Host tests cover read-only and denied mutations.
requirements.remaining: Part2 service-refusal execution, live request counters, denied-copy UI and unchanged-disk oracle remain open. Compilation cannot establish refusal at the actual native service boundary.

requirements.description: Keep history and location correct and understandable
requirements.observation: Native library flow exercises actual collections, names, revision history and restoration, backed by cold disk verification.
requirements.remaining: History dialog semantic reading order remains an ignored defect, and denied/recovery copy is still generic in cases. Human understanding is not established by pixel/script checks.

criteria.remaining: Native HiDPI/input progress is real and should be reported. Missing screen-reader chain, known compact/semantic defects and absent human task evidence keep U04 open.

requirements.description: Keyboard-only operation and focus
requirements.observation: Materiaal/window sessions have keyboard paths and native automated coverage; local semantics expose roles, focus and action descriptions.
requirements.remaining: Coverage is a bounded app/session subset, not all required native task flows; known History semantic order remains unresolved.

requirements.description: Native screen reader support
requirements.observation: ui/native provides an app-local bounded semantics tree, explicitly preparation for a future broker.
requirements.remaining: No OS-wide native accessibility broker/event channel and working screen reader chain is demonstrated; TTS/braille path and native task use remain open.

requirements.description: Scaling/zoom in the native chain
requirements.observation: Current 100%/200% native window/switcher evidence passes; scale2 66 phases has full retained report and serial.
requirements.remaining: Compact error status at 640x480@200% has a deliberately ignored clipping defect; these successful profiles do not establish every required layout.

requirements.description: Contrast and reduced motion in the native chain
requirements.observation: Native rendering has bounded appearance/semantics tests; browser UX-E contrast/media emulation is measured and explicitly simulation-only. Shell shows reduced motion fixed on.
requirements.remaining: No complete native/user-task acceptance for contrast and configurable reduced motion; browser CDP measurements cannot supply it.

requirements.description: Record accessibility user task tests
requirements.observation: An explicit protocol and task register exist.
requirements.remaining: No recorded representative human/native screen-reader task outcomes or resolution/retest evidence were found.

criteria.remaining: The native six-boot settings persistence success supersedes old blockers, but search S3, actual accounts/settings UI and known recovery text/layout defects remain functional gaps.

requirements.description: Native settings work and persist consistently
requirements.observation: Typed/revertible settings core is now an SDK workspace member. The volume adapter passes six cold boots: initialize/update, read-only recover, revert, damaged-newest fallback, both copies corrupt, unsupported schema refusal; unchanged read-only images and zero writes/flushes.
requirements.remaining: No user-changeable Settings app/UI or authenticated per-user scope. The shell's quick-settings page remains fixed/notices. Native persistence is a delivered subrequirement, not all system settings.

requirements.description: Local indexed search works natively
requirements.observation: SDK search core and 23-test volume adapter are integrated; S2 native binary/build and independent oracle/draft runner are present and CI-covered.
requirements.remaining: S3 has no kernel feature/case/build override. Current require_wiring exits1 naming those three missing edits. No native execution, native revocation, content tokens or interactive indexed-file search UI.

requirements.description: Account and session management work consistently
requirements.observation: Native shell has lock/guest routes and explicitly refuses local-user authentication instead of accepting credentials.
requirements.remaining: Real account service, personal authentication/unlock, profile/key separation and account management are absent. Guest route is not personal session acceptance.

requirements.description: Understandable error and recovery paths
requirements.observation: #472 contributes five active recovery cases covering uncertain/interrupted saves. Existing native recovery gates continue to pass.
requirements.remaining: Four deliberately ignored current defects: distinct Full/Quota text, known I/O text, Access/denial text, and compact200% failure-status clipping. The inherited History-order ignore is separate.

criteria.remaining: A study plan is delivered, but real participants, approved budgets and measured resolution are the missing original acceptance, not merely a paperwork refresh.

requirements.description: Agree and preregister representative core tasks and budgets
requirements.observation: U06-USABILITY-PROTOCOL.md provides tasks, success keys, proposed budgets, participant/privacy plan and route-validation/pilot rules.
requirements.remaining: Budgets/task-set approval, frozen candidate bundle, route verification and pilot are not completed; some core tasks remain not yet testable.

requirements.description: Representative users complete the agreed native tasks
requirements.observation: Native script evidence supplies a candidate subset of document/window tasks; browser UX-E is explicitly AI-only simulation verification.
requirements.remaining: No representative human study results were found. AI/CDP/QMP execution cannot count as participants completing tasks.

requirements.description: Measure and resolve friction, errors and visual inconsistency within budgets
requirements.observation: Protocol defines findings and retest records; host/native automated tests expose specific present defects.
requirements.remaining: No human measurement aggregates, accepted budget comparisons or human retest closure. Five ignored UI specs remain recorded functional issues.

criteria.remaining: Real authorized connection end-to-end evidence.

requirements.description: Address configuration
requirements.observation: DHCP DISCOVER/OFFER/SELECT/ACK applies lease through same transport; NAK withdraws and fresh lease acquired. Host expiry/no-default-DNS cases exist; three native extension cases pass exact main. Later than the 2eb1c63 snapshot, PR #485 (N02-T6) hosted libslirp case: QEMU's independent DHCP server leases the guest address (one ACK bound to the pcap).
requirements.remaining: Current execution uses controlled synthetic Ethernet peer.

requirements.description: Name resolution
requirements.observation: Lease-supplied A resolver with bounded TTL/negative cache/epoch invalidation; native A,NXDOMAIN,wrong-ID/wrong-port refusals and re-resolution after changed lease demonstrated. Later than the 2eb1c63 snapshot, PR #485 (N02-T6) hosted libslirp case: example.com resolved through the CI runner's real resolver; answer bound to the guest's own query ID/port in the pcap. N02-T6 NXDOMAIN slice (branch claude/n02-slirp-negative-dns-20261124): the reserved name missing.invalid returns NotFound in-guest and exactly one rcode-3 response without addresses, bound to its own query and name, appears on the wire; NXDOMAIN versus empty NOERROR is distinguished only by the pcap. The answer comes from the host-configured resolver via libslirp.
requirements.remaining: Real authorized resolver/interoperability scenario not established; DNS timeout, truncation and stale-response cases against a real resolver not run.

requirements.description: Routing
requirements.observation: Native off-link case uses DHCP router/default route and router MAC, with real guest packets verified by controlled peer. Later than the 2eb1c63 snapshot, PR #485 (N02-T6) hosted libslirp case: libslirp is router and DNS forwarder; HTTP to the router alias reaches a host-loopback oracle.
requirements.remaining: Single Python peer plays router/host/server; actual forwarding path not exercised.

requirements.description: Network transitions
requirements.observation: Actual QMP link down/up changes virtio-net STATUS; old configuration withdrawn, fresh lease and DNS acquired; transmit window checked unchanged while down.
requirements.remaining: Bounded single transition under emulation; real authorized connection transition not recorded.

requirements.description: Required protocols operate on real authorized connections
requirements.observation: Native IPv4/ARP/TCP/UDP/DHCP/DNS and HTTP fixture traffic execute; current reports explicitly scope synthetic localhost Ethernet. Later than the 2eb1c63 snapshot, PR #485 (N02-T6) hosted libslirp case adds DHCP, real-resolver DNS and HTTP through QEMU user networking (restrict=off, owner decision 24 Nov 2026, non-required job).
requirements.remaining: libslirp is QEMU user networking on the same host, not a physical or operator network; internet HTTP, NXDOMAIN/timeout against a real resolver and real connection transitions remain unproven.

criteria.remaining: Native provider and service/bootstrap; Native-authorized crypto randomness; Native peer/time policy and complete negative handshake evidence.

requirements.description: Maintained TLS and fixed hybrid profile implemented
requirements.observation: rustls0.23.46 profile module restricts TLS1.3/X25519MLKEM768/TLS13_AES_256_GCM_SHA384/ALPN;17 loopback+8 profile tests pass exact main; native-compatible library compiles.
requirements.remaining: No selected working native crypto provider/service/bootstrap; no native handshake.

requirements.description: Peer verification
requirements.observation: Exact DER/SPKI pins, mutual CertificateVerify proof of private-key possession, extra-chain rejection and ALPN gate exercised. Host positives use fixed time; pin is identity, hostname/roots/validity not consulted.
requirements.remaining: Native trusted time/peer model and certificate-validity/hostname requirements not implemented/proven.

requirements.description: Negative handshakes
requirements.observation: Wrong pins,impostor keys,missing client cert,wrong suite/ALPN,TLS1.2,unavailable time and RNG denial all pass host negatives; no released plaintext on negative handshake paths.
requirements.remaining: Execute required native handshakes, malformed/expired certificate cases on actual native TLS principal.

requirements.description: No silent insecure fallback and native-authorized randomness
requirements.observation: Classical-only server/client refused; library cannot configure missing hybrid group/suite. KeyServiceRandom covers rustls random calls in synthetic host tests; AWS-LC KEM/signing randomness bypasses it as host-only oracle.
requirements.remaining: Native provider RNG/platform route and fail-closed full-profile handshake absent.

criteria.remaining: Production issuer/permission route; Durable revocation and generation-bound regrant; Delegated helper subgrants.

requirements.description: Per-process and destination permissions enforced natively
requirements.observation: Two actual app principals have kernel-bound ingress and restricted destination grants; wrong destinations/caller requests denied; packet oracle rejects unexpected traffic.
requirements.remaining: Production issuer/user permission route is absent; current manifest-fixed clients/grants only.

requirements.description: Revocation enforced on active/new operations and visible in traffic
requirements.observation: Native revoke sends authenticated policy command, aborts live appA TCP and denies five retained-handle operations; peer observes RST and no further unauthorized appA frames; appB unaffected.
